findings.reason: The protected source is an expert-quality Sprague-Grundy solution. It decomposes the immutable minus-separated plus runs, builds each run game's mex recurrence once, xor-combines the independent components, and returns the standard nonzero-position test. Its concepts and structure are clear, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 294 and its Python state-string-to-boolean optimal-play contract. The Reference preserves the move and terminal-loss rules, both examples in order and the sole explanation, all three constraints including the 20-consecutive-plus limit, and the runtime-analysis follow-up.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064318175. It and the app-local source have identical run extraction, maximum-run bound, bottom-up Grundy recurrence, reachable xor set, mex loop, component xor, and nonzero result; only the required wrapper and type syntax differ.

The former largest tier used 24 consecutive plus signs and violated the source maximum of 20. Legal 5/10/20-run tiers now span 4x and exercise the full allowed run domain. The current source passes at +0.02 relative exponent and 1.00x largest ratio; correct full-board recursion with memoization passes every output but fails only scaling at +3.96 and 272.53x.

The manifest and Approach now distinguish complete state length m from maximum run length n, yielding O(m + n^2) time and O(m) space for the actual protected implementation. The explanation derives every split, mex, xor composition, cancellation, and the short-run base cases.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving both examples and their explanation presence, all three constraints, the source-native follow-up, and the zero-visual structure.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact states and optimal-play results.
The previous invented pair row is now a trial, and the previously hidden unequal-run and no-pair behaviors are visible.
The suite covers minimum and maximum complete-state lengths, both one-character terminals, the only-pair win, overlapping moves, and a losing five-plus run.
Independent components cover two equal pair runs, two equal triple runs, three equal pair runs, unequal runs with nonzero xor, and unequal run lengths whose Grundy values still cancel.
Minus padding and separated singleton pluses verify that immutable separators create independent games and that runs shorter than two contribute zero.
Each authored result was independently evaluated by full minimax; the protected source also matched that oracle on 42,766 exhaustive and seeded legal states, including all benchmark inputs.
All 14 correctness cases are visible; the unchanged legal plus-run lengths 5, 10, and 20 remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
